_meta.note: Industry, peers, street, ownership, stock, moat, critiques, gaps and conflicts for Laurus Labs. Only sources published on or before 30-Sep-2026; later facts are in research/updates/later-facts.json.

cdmo.src: Laurus Sep-2026 investor presentation (company-cited industry estimates); HDFC Securities sector thematic 6-Jan-2026 (Frost & Sullivan, Evaluate Pharma)

industry.drivers: Innovators outsource more manufacturing (24% in 2024 to 39% by 2029, HDFC Securities), China+1 and the US BIOSECURE Act push work to India, AI-designed molecules are more complex to make (Laurus Head CDMO, 30-Apr-2026), and GLP-1/peptide demand needs new capacity.

arv.laurusShareOfPatients: about one-third of the global HIV population
arv.outlook: Stable market supported by multilateral funding; dolutegravir use steady for the next couple of years; long-acting injectables face adherence and retention hurdles (company, Q4FY26 presentation)
arv.lenacapavir: Gilead granted royalty-free licences for twice-yearly injectable lenacapavir to Dr. Reddy's, Emcure, Eva Pharma, Ferozsons, Hetero and Mylan for 120 countries (2-Oct-2024); Laurus is not a licensee
arv.src: q4fy26ppt p.26; q4fy26 call; Gilead press release 2-Oct-2024

industry.costs: The West Asia war (from late Feb-2026) raised solvent prices; Laurus saw 'some impact' in Q4FY26 and 'some pressure' in Q1FY27 but no supply disruption (calls of 30-Apr and 24-Jul-2026).

excluded.LAURUSLABS: Self; also boom-bust EPS (FY21-23 ARV/CDMO peak, FY24 trough) with P/E above 100x inside the window (PLAYBOOK §7c).
excluded.LUPIN: Loss years inside the five-year window distort its median (PLAYBOOK §7c).
excluded.BIOCON: One-off and boom-bust EPS; P/E above 100x inside the window (PLAYBOOK §7c).
excluded.DRREDDY: gRevlimid windfall FY23-26 then the cliff; Q4FY26 EPS Rs2.65 (PLAYBOOK §7c).

peers.notes: Pharma peer set set on 23-Nov-2026 (PLAYBOOK §7c). Laurus is outside the set, so its factor is the median of all nine peers: +8.2% (per-peer re-ratings rounded to 0.1pt; +8.19% unrounded). Including the five other excluded names (all 14 others) gives +5.4%, shown as a sensitivity only. The EV/EBITDA analogue for the same nine peers (trailing EV/EBITDA at the 30-Sep close vs the five-year median of Screener's 'EV Multiple') is +7.5%.

brokers.thesis: 'Blockbuster beat led by CDMO momentum'; EPS raised 21%/16%; FY27 capex Rs20bn backed by contracts; most Phase III CDMO supplies to turn commercial
CDMO run-rate up from Rs220-250 cr to ~Rs800 cr a quarter in two years, broad-based unlike the earlier one-off order; premium justified by sustained capex and delivery
CDMO revenue CAGR 43% over three years to ~50% of sales by FY30E; capex stays elevated; EPS raised 11%/18%
'All optimism baked in to valuations'; multiple raised to 55x (from 50x), in line with Divi's
Growth momentum to continue as more late-stage CDMO molecules move to commercial manufacturing (its Oct-2025 note used 45x Sep-27E EPS)
Upgraded from Hold; highest target on the street; EBITDA margin near 30% by FY28 (secondary summary; note not seen)
CDMO the primary growth driver; higher-margin CDMO mix keeps lifting profitability (secondary summary; note not seen)
Still sees ~33% downside after raising its target post-results (CNBC-TV18 report)
Maintained Hold; target raised after Q1FY27
Initiation: CDMO to drive growth and margins but the stock had re-rated 80%+; generic APIs muted (mature ARV); implies 51x P/E. No post-Q1 update found
CDMO ramp-up awaited; 50% CDMO by FY30 target maintained. Pre-Q1, no later note found

consensus.what: LSEG (via Reuters on Zerodha): 13 analysts, average rating 'hold', median target Rs1,045
Tracker cited by AskFuzz: 19 analysts, 11 Buy / 4 Hold / 4 Sell, average 12-month target Rs1,630

street.methodCount: Disclosed methods among notes standing on 30-Sep-2026: P/E 4 (Motilal Oswal, BOBCAPS, Choice via PEG, Sharekhan), EV/EBITDA 2 (ICICI Securities, HDFC Securities). Not disclosed: DRChoksey, InCred, DAM, Kotak, Jefferies.

moat.evidence: Supplies ARV APIs/formulations for about one-third of the world's HIV patients; ~Rs2,800 cr of ARV revenue at full utilisation; backward integration from intermediates
8,800 KL of reactors on fungible standard designs; validation at commercial scale on the same equipment train; three NCE APIs commercialised in 18 months; flow chemistry, biocatalysis, high-potency
21 USFDA inspections since inception, EIRs at all key sites, no active warning letter or import alert (CARE, Jun-2026); zero recalls in five years; 132 audits in FY26 without critical findings
>125 active projects, a new big-pharma client in Q1FY27; but customers, molecules and contract sizes are undisclosed and the FY23 order shows how fast CDMO revenue can vanish
Once Laurus is filed in a customer's dossier, a change needs re-validation and regulatory approval, but only for the life of each molecule
ARV tenders and generic APIs are price-led with Chinese and Indian rivals; Laurus is not a lenacapavir licensee
Bio ~Rs200 cr revenue and Rs7 cr profit; CAR-T via a 35% associate; ADC assets pre-clinical; management: returns 4-5 years away

critiques: The price already pays for the plan: ~66x our Sep-28E EPS and ~72x FY28E against a ~36x own forward median since 2021; BOBCAPS calls it 'all optimism baked in'
BOBCAPS (Hold, 27-Jul-2026), Kotak (Sell, Rs1,125), HDFC Securities (Reduce, Jan-2026)

CDMO revenue is lumpy: the FY23 purchase order lifted small-molecule CDMO to Rs2,167 cr before it fell to Rs922 cr in FY24; 45% of Q1FY27 CDMO revenue was Phase III/launch supplies that can pause once customers stock up
CARE (inherent volatility), MOSL and analysts on the Q1FY27 call
Capex runs ahead of cash: Rs2,000 cr in FY27 (~24% of sales) after Rs4,300 cr in FY22-26; asset turn ~0.9x; free cash flow turns negative in FY27E and debt rises
CARE, HDFC Securities, Q1FY27 call (capex questions)
ARV is mature and exposed to donor funding and to long-acting injectables; Laurus is not among Gilead's six lenacapavir licensees
Advanced biologics (gene therapy, ADCs, CAR-T) and Laurus Bio consume capital and R&D (5.8% of sales in Q1FY27) with returns 4-5 years away by management's own account
Disclosure is thin: no customers, molecules, phase-wise pipeline or segment margins; constant-currency growth was not clarified on the Q1 call
Much of FY26-27 margin expansion came from gross margin (raw-material softening, mix); operating leverage is only starting while new plants add fixed costs
Analysts on the Q4FY26 call; Choice, BOBCAPS
gaps: Customers, molecules, contract values and the phase split of the >125 CDMO projects are confidential; we model CDMO only as a revenue line.

FY21 small-molecule CDMO revenue is not legible in the company chart (CDMO incl. Bio Rs528 cr by difference); FY22-24 Bio revenue is derived by difference; the FY23/FY24 ARV split is our reading of the company chart.
Q1-Q3FY25 API, FDF and Bio revenue are back-calculated from MOSL's FY26 growth rates and reconcile to the FY25 totals; they are not company-tabled figures.

Valuation methods not found for DRChoksey (Jul-2026), InCred, DAM Capital, Kotak and Jefferies; InCred and DAM targets come from a secondary summary (AskFuzz, 24-Jul-2026), not the notes. No post-Q1 note found for HDFC Securities or Sharekhan; their pre-Q1 calls are shown as standing.
No Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley, Citi, Nomura, Nuvama or Axis note dated on or before 30-Sep-2026 was found (Nuvama initiated in Oct-2026: later-facts.json).
The BOBCAPS Q1FY27 PDF was refused to a direct download (site firewall); it was read through the standard WebFetch tool, with no headers changed. Flagged for the reviewer.
Jun-2026 named holders (>1%) and pledge status were not retrieved; Mar-2026 figures are used.
Peptide capacity, Unit 7 block sizes, capex by project and capacity utilisation by site are not disclosed.
Constant-currency growth for Q1FY27 was not clarified (CFO said ~2%, then referred it to IR).
Laurus Bio's Q1FY27 loss implied by the minority line (Rs6 cr) is not separately disclosed.
conflicts: Company EBITDA Rs1,826 cr in FY26 (Rs644 cr in Q1FY27) includes other income; Screener's operating profit Rs1,785 cr (Rs638 cr) excludes it and adds back the Rs7.5 cr loss on sale of PPE. We use Screener's basis; the company's '>30% from FY27+' guidance is on its own basis, ~0.3-0.7pt higher.

Company: Rs59 cr, Rs0.9 EPS; AR note 18: Rs58.85 cr; Screener: Rs57 cr pre-tax / Rs39 cr after tax (Rs0.72 a share). We use Screener's schedule for EPS before exceptional items, consistently across years.

The AR has no exceptional line; Screener shows -Rs7 cr (loss on sale of PPE); MOSL shows Rs21 cr of extraordinary items in Q3-Q4FY26 (likely incl. the Labour Codes gratuity charge). We use Screener's -Rs7 cr; it changes FY26 EPS by Rs0.11.
CARE (3-Jul-2026): ~Rs3,000-3,500 cr over FY27-29 (Rs1,000-1,500 cr a year). Company (24-Jul and 18-Sep-2026): Rs2,000 cr in FY27 and >Rs3,000 cr over FY27-28. We follow the later company figures.
Rs368 cr attributable to owners (company, EPS Rs6.8) vs Rs362 cr total profit (Screener 'Net Profit'); patched to the attributable figure.
Company presentation: CDMO 43% of revenue (incl. Bio); brokers quote 41% (small molecules only). Both are right on their definitions.
